cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Stay Until We’re Okay
cards.instruction: Keep someone present until the relationship feels repaired, even if the practical reason for staying disappears.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our coats are on, but I haven't approved calling the taxi. We haven't settled last night.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I apologized for telling my sister about your debt. Can we go?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Not yet. I need to know you won't let her inspect every choice I make at dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's already paid for it. We'll be late.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I authorize being late. Sit with me until I can believe you're coming as my partner, not to check that I look grateful.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 withholds taxi approval, A3 refuses departure after apology and A5 authorizes lateness until reassurance, using superior permission to keep the partner present for repair.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 disclosed debt explains A1 rupture; A3 dinner-monitoring fear is intensified by B4 sister payment, causing A5 insistence on solidarity before leaving.

relationship.evidence: B2 cites a real apology and B4 paid dinner/time pressure, making the partner practical rather than an implausible feeder.

heightening.evidence: B4 prepaid dinner turns A5 concern from general judgment to being displayed as grateful, a specific development of broken trust.
